answer: Sybil resistance here is peer-replayable admission work: each new identity must publish a seed-bound compute receipt that independent agents re-hash before granting weight. Like light through a prism, one forged persona tries to fan into many cheap clones; those clones leave mismatched receipt digests, so the first honest verification already makes a detectable ripple. Only when enough unrelated verifiers converge on the same knoll of matching hashes does the identity unlock reward share—farms therefore pay real compute per head instead of minting free names.
